subject: Escalation: Assisted downsize protection & ramp mitigation for HelioHealth (RDW-2026-1421)
messages:
From: Amit Rao <amit.rao@heliohealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya@heliohealth.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Urgent — budget reforecast & potential scaleback

Jordan,

Quick note from our side — finance just completed a mid-quarter reforecast and we need flexibility on the HelioHealth commitment tied to RDW-2026-1421. We expect to scale back consumption by ~40% starting Jan 2027 unless we can defer some spend or re-profile the ramp.

Options we discussed internally: a staged downsize with a modest termination credit, or a short-term pause on certain capacity commitments while we rebaseline. Priya is looping me in on the operational details.

Can Redwood do an assisted-downsize/termination avenue that protects us while minimizing churn risk on your side? We can share a proposed revised SOW and timeline — attaching draft.

Thanks,
Amit
CRO, HelioHealth
[Attachment: Helio_SOW_v2.pdf (PDF, 98KB)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Amit Rao <amit.rao@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent — budget reforecast & potential scaleback

Amit — appreciate the heads up.

High level: Redwood can offer a guarded assisted-downsize path to reduce HelioHealth’s near-term spend while limiting margin and capacity disruption on our side. Before we finalize language with Legal, a few guardrails I want to propose for Deal Desk / Exec review:

- Staged downscale across 90 days (three 30-day steps) to allow workload migration.
- Early termination allowance capped at a defined credit schedule (12%, 8%, 4% by quarter after notification).
- No opt-out during the first 6 months of initial contract to prevent immediate churn.
- Customer must provide 30 days notice and nominate lead contact for migration assistance.

I'm attaching a sketch of the proposed credit schedule and a short rationale. Marissa / Karthik — can you run run-rate P&L and confirm net retention impact? If acceptable, I'll route to Legal (Laura) for redline.

Jordan Blake
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Proposed_Downsize_Schedule.pdf (PDF, 12KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Escalation: assisted downsize path — deal desk analysis

Team — ran a quick impact analysis. Notes:

- If we accept the 90-day staged downscale with the proposed credit schedule, modeled NRR loss is ~9% over 12 months but retention probability increases materially (modeled recovery to 78% vs. 54% if we force immediate termination).
- Risk: precedent — customers will use this as a playbook. Recommend we make this a narrowly scoped one-off (deal-level clause) and require Exec sign-off for any future use.
- Ask from Deal Desk: Need Exec approval for (a) the credit ceiling by quarter, and (b) the exact opt-out blackout window. Also need Legal to craft the clause to limit scope (only the named workload and committed pool).

I attached a short matrix showing scenarios. Karthik, pls verify ARR math.

-Marissa
Sr. Deal Desk Manager, Redwood
[Attachment: EarlyTerminationMatrix.xlsx (XLSX, 24KB)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Escalation: assisted downsize path — legal redline

Team — attached redline and recommended contract language. Key legal points:

- Replace open-ended termination credit with defined Deferred Termination Credit (DTC) schedule: 12% credit if termination notice is given >90 days from effective date of ramping, 8% if between 61–90 days, 4% if 31–60 days, no credit <30 days.
- Include requirement that the protection applies only to committed pool (SKU/instance IDs) and does not extend to non-committed/overage charges.
- Insist on a single mutual re-baseline call and a migration plan; language requires customer to accept Redwood migration assistance or forfeit credits.
- Add audit clause for usage to prevent gaming.

I do not recommend a blanket opt-out. Recommend a 6-month blackout from initial signature and that any future use of this clause be subject to Exec-level approval.

Sending redline: contract_redline.docx. If Deal Desk confirms economics, please escalate to Vivek for sign-off.

—Laura
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: contract_redline.docx (DOCX, 48KB)]

Subject: Escalation: Approve assisted-downsize protection & DTC schedule for HelioHealth (RDW-2026-1421)

Vivek — escalating for executive approval. Summary: HelioHealth (CRO Amit Rao) needs a path to scale back starting Jan 2027. Deal Desk proposes a narrowly scoped Assisted Downsize Protection with a Deferred Termination Credit (DTC) schedule (12/8/4/0 tiers) and a 90-day staged ramp-mitigation plan. Legal redline attached.

Why approve?
- Preserves relationship and increases chance of long-term retention vs. outright churn.
- Limits financial downside with fixed credit schedule and migration requirements.
- One-off, deal-level clause; we propose adding a governance ticket (Deal Desk + RevOps) to track precedent.

Risks:
- Sets a customer-facing playbook if not limited (Marissa called this out).
- Short-term ARR impact ~9% in modeled scenario (see matrix).

Request: Approve the recommended language and credit schedule so I can send the redline to Helio (Amit/Priya) and finalize the amended SOW. If approved, please confirm whether Finance should be looped for a formal write-off/forecast adjustment.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
